content.comment_body: [product_name] Ver[version_no] [product_name] Ver[version_no] I'm new to [product_name]. I've been reviewing the "Swimming Pool" and "[product_name] Cloud Connect" examples. I'm attempting to build a very basic demo—a single button toggling a light. In both examples from [company_name], a 'Digital Value' object indicates light status. My question: Where can I locate the 'Digital Value' component? I see 'Push Button' and 'Switch Button,' but not 'Digital Value.' I'm sure there's a straightforward solution, but I'm puzzled!

Hi [user_name], Regarding your question, I don't have a direct answer since it's unclear to me as well. While researching, I found this post: [url] The post offers an alternative for achieving the function you're seeking. I realize it's not the detailed answer you want—I hope someone else can provide it—but if not, at least this gives you an option. Best regards and good luck!

The issue is that the swimming pool example was created using the initial version of [product_name]. That version only had the digital value component. In newer versions, 'digital value' was replaced by 'switch button.' Users have previously raised concerns about the lack of push button functionality in earlier [product_name] releases ([version_no]). As a result, [company_name] removed the digital value feature and introduced two new button components in version [version_no].

Here's what the components pane looks like in [product_name] [version_no]: In the 'Digital' section, you only see the Digital Value. And here's the pane in version [version_no]: In the 'Digital' section, you now see the Push Button and Switch Button.

Thanks [user_name] for clarifying. To achieve what I'm aiming for, I should: • use a Switch Button • select a block type like M or Q • make sure the Writable flag is disabled • customize the default ON and OFF images as needed

If you intend to modify a variable's state, don't disable the 'Writeable' checkbox—it's essential to keep it enabled. You can only directly adjust the state of a marker or output if they're not linked to input-side logic.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about changes in [product_name], notably the removal of the 'Digital Value' component and its replacement with 'Push Button' and 'Switch Button' options. Insufficient documentation and unclear migration paths between software versions lead to initial confusion and difficulties, especially when trying to recreate older example projects. These version discrepancies create discoverability and consistency problems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to find a 'Digital Value' component in the latest [product_name] version to follow previous examples and easily manage or display digital states, as was possible before.
